ctwPassages.topic: city seed-lending program for neighborhood gardeners

segments.text: The city library now runs a program that lets residents borrow packets of vegetable and flower seeds for their own yards. Visitors

sprout successfully across gardens. At the end of the season, borrowers are encouraged to save extra stock from healthy plants and return it to the shelves. The habit has grown popular among neighbors who share a plot nearby, since it lowers the cost of starting new beds each spring.

gaps.explanationZh: 前文提到訪客到圖書館借種子,此句描述他們的行為:先「瀏覽」(browse)依類型排列的種子選項,才能決定要拿哪一包,語意上與後面「sorted by type」及「then sign a form」的動作順序相符,故填 browse。
browse 的受詞須為可供瀏覽的「品項總稱」,selection 指圖書館提供、依類型排列的種子「選項/品項組合」,與前句 borrow packets of vegetable and flower seeds 呼應,故填 selection。
sorted by type 是固定搭配,表示「依照…分類」,by 在此引導分類依據(type),為介系詞用法,故填 by。
句中描述訪客的動作順序:先瀏覽選項,「接著」(then)簽表格,再拿走種子包,then 表示時間上的先後承接,故填 then。
此處描述「簽表格」發生在「拿種子包回家」之前,before 表示時間先後,與前面 then sign a form 的動作順序一致,故填 before。
taking a packet home 呼應首句 borrow ... seeds for their own yards,訪客把種子帶「回家」種在自己院子,故填 home。
工作人員的職責是把每次借閱「記錄」下來(record each checkout in a log),與後面 in a log(記錄本)搭配,故填 record。
checkout 指「借出/領取」這項交易本身,呼應前文的 borrow 動作,是 record 的受詞,說明工作人員記錄的是每一次的借閱紀錄,故填 checkout。
工作人員記錄借閱資料的目的是「追蹤」(tracking)哪些品種發芽成功,tracking 與後面 which varieties sprout successfully 語意連貫,說明持續觀察的行為,故填 tracking。
varieties 指不同「品種」的種子,呼應開頭 vegetable and flower seeds 的多樣性,說明工作人員追蹤的是哪些「品種」發芽良好,故填 varieties。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: The city library now runs a program that lets residents borrow packets of vegetable and flower seeds for their own yards. Visitors browse the selection sorted by type, then sign a form before taking a packet home. Staff record each checkout in a log, tracking which varieties sprout successfully across gardens. At the end of the season, borrowers are encouraged to save extra stock from healthy plants and return it to the shelves. The habit has grown popular among neighbors who share a plot nearby, since it lowers the cost of starting new beds each spring.

segments.text: The airport now runs a shuttle bus service that connects the main terminal to nearby hotels around the clock. Vehicles

land close together. Staff study the arrival board each morning and add extra runs during those busy waves so travelers do not stand outside for long. The schedule change has shortened waiting periods near the pickup zone, and new signs at the stop display upcoming departure times. Officials say the updated system feels smoother than the old fixed timetable, which ignored actual traffic patterns.

gaps.explanationZh: 主詞是複數的 Vehicles,後面接原形動詞表示習慣性動作,故用 depart(而非 departs);depart from the curb 表示「從路邊出發」,與後文 every fifteen minutes 的班次描述相符。
the curb 使用定冠詞是因為情境上的唯一性——指的是這座機場唯一的一個接送區路邊,而非前一句提過的特定地點(前一句只提到接駁車連接航廈與附近飯店,並未提及路邊)。讀者能從機場接駁車情境推知這是「那個」固定的上下車地點,因此用 the 而非 a。
every fifteen minutes 是表示頻率的固定搭配,every + 時間長度表示「每隔多久」一次,用來說明車輛發車的間隔頻率。
fifteen 是數詞,後面須接複數名詞 minutes 作為單位,fifteen minutes 表示「十五分鐘」這段時間長度,對應 every 所需的時間單位。
most of the day 是固定用法,表示「一天中的大部分時間」,用來說明車輛在多數時間都維持固定的十五分鐘班距。
the day 在此指說話者與讀者共同理解、當下討論脈絡中的那一天(即接駁車運行的一整天),屬於語境上可辨識的特定指涉,故用定冠詞 the。
though 引導讓步子句,用來連接前面「多數時間維持固定班距」與後面「班距會依情況調整」這兩個略帶對比的訊息,表示雖然如此、但仍有例外。
主詞是複數的 drivers,同樣需要原形動詞,故用 adjust(而非 adjusts);adjust pace 表示「調整發車節奏」,呼應後面 when several flights land close together 所描述的情況。
when 引導時間子句,說明司機調整節奏的觸發時機,即「當數個航班幾乎同時抵達時」,精確對應後文 several flights land close together 的描述。
flights 是 land 的主詞,several flights land close together 表示「數個航班相繼、幾乎同時降落」,說明造成接駁車需要調整班距的原因,與前文 several flights land 的情境一致。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: The airport now runs a shuttle bus service that connects the main terminal to nearby hotels around the clock. Vehicles depart from the curb every fifteen minutes for most of the day, though drivers adjust pace when several flights land close together. Staff study the arrival board each morning and add extra runs during those busy waves so travelers do not stand outside for long. The schedule change has shortened waiting periods near the pickup zone, and new signs at the stop display upcoming departure times. Officials say the updated system feels smoother than the old fixed timetable, which ignored actual traffic patterns.

academic.title: Balancing Peak and Off-Peak Train Fares
academic.text:
Regional train operators face a familiar problem: commuter trains are packed during the early morning and late afternoon rush, yet nearly empty in the middle of the day. To smooth out this uneven demand, many operators have adopted time-based pricing, charging lower fares for tickets purchased outside the busiest hours. A commuter traveling at 10 a.m. might pay forty percent less than one traveling at 8 a.m., even though the trip itself is identical.

This approach works because train travel is what economists call price-sensitive for many riders. Commuters with fixed office hours have little choice but to travel during peak times regardless of cost, but students, retirees, and workers with flexible schedules often shift their trips when a discount is available. As more of these flexible travelers move to off-peak hours, peak-hour trains become less crowded, while off-peak trains, once nearly empty, begin generating meaningful revenue instead of running at a loss.

Critics argue that fare differences can feel unfair to riders who have no choice but to travel at peak times, since they end up paying the highest price for the most crowded service. Operators counter that without off-peak discounts, the whole network would need higher fares across the board to cover costs, so nearly everyone benefits from the arrangement in the end.

questions.stem: According to the passage, why do train operators offer lower off-peak fares?

options.text: To comply with a fare pricing regulation
To encourage riders to shift trip times
To lower maintenance costs on older trains
To attract new tourists to the network

questions.explanationZh: 文中指出離峰優惠是為了讓乘客改到人少的時段搭乘，藉此平衡尖峰與離峰人數，而非為了降低維修成本、符合票價法規或吸引觀光客。

questions.stem: The word "price-sensitive" in paragraph 2 is closest in meaning to

options.text: unable to pay full fare
unaffected by ticket price
responsive to changes in cost
influenced by advertising claims

questions.explanationZh: 「price-sensitive」意指乘客的行為會隨價格變動而改變，對應下文彈性行程的乘客因折扣改變搭乘時間，而非受廣告影響、無力負擔車資，或對票價毫不在意。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that riders with fixed office hours

options.text: rarely choose to travel by train at all
often pay less than flexible commuters do
still travel at peak hours despite the cost
receive a discount to offset the inconvenience

questions.explanationZh: 文中提到固定上班時間的乘客不論票價高低仍須在尖峰時段搭乘，可推知這類乘客通常仍在尖峰時段搭乘，而非付費較少、很少搭火車或獲得折扣補償。

questions.stem: How does the third paragraph relate to the second paragraph?

options.text: It moves on to an unrelated ticketing topic
It restates the economic theory from before
It adds further evidence for the earlier claim
It raises an objection to the earlier benefits

questions.explanationZh: 第三段提出對離峰定價的質疑，屬於對第二段所述效益的反駁，而非重述理論、提供支持證據或轉向無關的售票科技話題。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.text: To explain how and why time-based train pricing works, along with a criticism of it
To recommend that all fares be made equal
To criticize regional train operators for unfair pricing
To compare train travel with other forms of transportation

questions.explanationZh: 全文先說明尖峰離峰定價如何運作及其經濟原理，接著提出對此策略的批評，主旨在於解釋此定價方式的運作與其爭議，而非單純批評營運商、比較交通方式或主張票價齊一。

segments.text: The old clock tower in the town square finally works again after many years of silence. Workers

anniversary celebration. Leaders chose this date because the community turned one hundred fifty years old. On the day of the event, people will gather at the site. They hope to hear it ring once more. A local carpenter who grew up nearby led most of the careful work. She said the project felt personal because her grandfather once cared for the same landmark long ago.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處主詞是 Workers，後面接的是表示花費時間的片語「months + Ving」，故需要 spend 的過去式 spent，與前一句「finally works again」的過去時態一致，表示工人們「花費」數月時間進行維修。
spent months 後面須接動名詞表示「花時間做某事」，fixing 與後面的 cleaning 為對等的動名詞結構（fixing the gears and cleaning the bell），描述工人具體做的兩件事之一：修理齒輪。
fixing 的受詞須是鐘塔內會損壞、需要修理的機械零件，gears（齒輪）正是驅動時鐘運作的核心機械部件，與主題「鐘塔維修」高度相關。
與 fixing 並列的第二個動名詞，由 and 連接（fixing the gears and cleaning the bell），描述工人所做的另一項工作：清潔鐘（bell）。
cleaning 的受詞需是鐘塔內部會需要清潔的物件，bell（鐘）呼應下文「hope to hear it ring once more」，指出他們清理的正是會發出鳴響聲的鐘。
此處為新句的開頭，主詞是「repair」這件事，需搭配定冠詞 The 指稱前文已提到、特定的那次「修復工程」（the repair）。
主詞 The repair 需要一個過去式動詞來說明其完成狀態，finished 表示「（修復工程）完成」，並與後方 in time for 呼應，指工程準時完工。
finished 之後接固定片語 in time for，表示「及時趕上」，此處指修復工程正好趕在特別的週年慶典之前完成。
承接 in time 的固定搭配 in time for + N，for 引出所趕上的對象，即後方的 special anniversary celebration（特別的週年慶典）。
special 修飾 anniversary celebration，呼應下一句說明社區屆滿一百五十週年，強調這是別具意義、特殊的紀念慶典，而非普通活動。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: The old clock tower in the town square finally works again after many years of silence. Workers spent months fixing the gears and cleaning the bell inside. The repair finished just in time for a special anniversary celebration. Leaders chose this date because the community turned one hundred fifty years old. On the day of the event, people will gather at the site. They hope to hear it ring once more. A local carpenter who grew up nearby led most of the careful work. She said the project felt personal because her grandfather once cared for the same landmark long ago.

academic.title: How Study Partnerships Form Among Students
academic.text:
Many college students find a study partner without ever planning to. Researchers who studied this pattern noticed that it usually starts with something simple: two students happen to sit near each other in the same class for several weeks in a row. Because they already share a class schedule, meeting up to review notes feels easy and requires little extra effort.

The library often becomes the natural meeting spot for these new study pairs. It is quiet, it is open late, and both students are already used to going there between classes. Over time, a pair that first met by chance may begin setting regular times to meet, especially as exams get closer.

These informal partnerships tend to be different from study groups that a teacher organizes. Because the two students chose each other, they usually feel more comfortable asking basic questions or admitting they are confused about something. Researchers found that students in these self-formed pairs often report feeling less stressed before exams, even when their test scores do not change much. The simple act of having someone to review material with, it seems, matters as much for confidence as it does for learning content itself.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what often starts a study partnership?

options.text: A teacher assigning students to specific study partners
Attending a mandatory academic orientation session together
Meeting for the first time during final exams week
Two students sitting near each other for weeks

questions.explanationZh: 文中提到夥伴關係通常始於兩名學生連續數週坐在同一堂課附近，並非老師指派、考試週才認識，或迎新活動促成的。

questions.stem: The word "informal" in paragraph 3 most nearly means

options.text: clearly unfriendly in tone
carelessly put together
not officially organized
strictly academic in focus

questions.explanationZh: 「informal」在此指非正式、非由他人安排組成的夥伴關係，對應與教師安排的讀書小組做對比，並非指規劃不佳、不友善或學術性的。

questions.stem: It can be inferred that students in self-formed study pairs feel comfortable asking basic questions because

options.text: the library staff mediates any confusion between them
they deliberately chose a partner they already trust
their professor grades them individually each week
the university requires each partner to submit a report afterward

questions.explanationZh: 文中指出因為是自己選擇的夥伴，學生較願意問基本問題，可推知這份自在感來自彼此本來就熟識、自願組隊，而非因規定繳交報告、圖書館協調或教授評分。

questions.stem: How does the second paragraph relate to the first paragraph?

options.text: It describes where these partnerships often continue meeting
It briefly summarizes every idea in the entire passage
It directly contradicts the main claim presented earlier
It shifts entirely to describing library operating hours and staff duties

questions.explanationZh: 第二段接續第一段提到的巧遇組隊情況，進一步說明這類夥伴通常在圖書館持續固定見面，是延伸說明而非反駁、離題或做總結。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.text: To criticize teacher-organized study groups
To describe how informal study partnerships form and how students benefit from them
To argue that library hours should be extended
To compare test scores across different universities

questions.explanationZh: 全文說明非正式讀書夥伴關係如何自然形成、以及它們為學生帶來的信心與情緒益處，主旨在描述此現象與其效益，而非批評正式小組、主張圖書館政策或比較成績。

segments.text: Over several months, a commuter methodically refined the walking route she took to work each morning. Rather

the most minutes. She discovered that a slightly longer detour avoided a notoriously slow crossing, saving a noticeable amount of time on average. She also learned that leaving slightly earlier let her reach a crucial intersection before a wave of office workers converged there. Combining these adjustments, she reduced her total commute by nearly twenty minutes each week, a gain that felt disproportionate to the modest effort involved.

gaps.explanationZh: 此處為「Rather than + Ving」的固定搭配，表示「與其⋯不如」，用來對比她並非走最短路徑，而是採取更講究的方式規劃路線，因此須填入 than。
following 之後接的是特定、唯一的「最短路徑」（the shortest path），指涉明確、聽者可辨識的對象，故需定冠詞 the。
the shortest 之後須接名詞才能構成完整的受詞片語，並與後文「計時每一段路程」呼應，指她原本要走的那條路線，故為 path。
主詞 she 之後需要一個過去式動詞，對應前一句「refined」、「methodically」等背景所鋪陳的行為模式：她針對路程的每一段進行「計時」，故填入 timed。
timed each 之後須接單數可數名詞作受詞，指她把「旅程」拆成一段段來計時，故填入 segment，並與後方 of her journey 語意相符。
segment of 之後須接所有格來說明「誰的」旅程，主詞為 she，故對應所有格代名詞 her，指她自己的通勤旅程。
此處以分詞構句補充說明她計時的同時做了什麼，動作與主句同時發生且主詞一致（she），故用現在分詞 noting，表示「同時注意到」。
noting where 之後需接一個名詞作為她「注意到」的內容，此處指「交通壅塞」造成時間耗損，故填入 congestion，並與 or mistimed signals 並列，同為導致延誤的原因。
此處與 congestion 並列，指另一種造成延誤的原因——「不同步／時機不對的號誌」，signals 前需要形容詞修飾，故填入 mistimed，呼應主題「計時」與「時機」的核心概念。
主詞為 congestion or mistimed signals，其後需要動詞說明這些因素「造成」了最多的時間損失，故填入 cost，與 the most minutes 搭配表示「耗費最多分鐘」。

ctwPassages.sourceParagraph: Over several months, a commuter methodically refined the walking route she took to work each morning. Rather than following the shortest path, she timed each segment of her journey, noting where congestion or mistimed signals cost the most minutes. She discovered that a slightly longer detour avoided a notoriously slow crossing, saving a noticeable amount of time on average. She also learned that leaving slightly earlier let her reach a crucial intersection before a wave of office workers converged there. Combining these adjustments, she reduced her total commute by nearly twenty minutes each week, a gain that felt disproportionate to the modest effort involved.

academic.title: Hydration Timing and Muscle Recovery After Exercise
academic.text:
Athletes have long been advised to replace fluids lost during exercise, but recent research suggests that the timing of rehydration, not merely its total volume, meaningfully influences how quickly muscles recover. In a series of controlled trials, researchers compared athletes who consumed fluids steadily throughout a two-hour recovery window against athletes who consumed an identical volume all at once immediately after finishing exercise.

Muscle biopsies revealed that the steady-intake group replenished glycogen, the stored form of carbohydrate muscles rely on for fuel, at a measurably faster rate than the immediate-bolus group, despite both groups ultimately consuming the same amount of fluid and carbohydrate. Researchers attribute this difference to gradual absorption: when large volumes are consumed rapidly, a portion passes through the digestive system before nutrients can be fully absorbed, whereas smaller, spaced intervals allow the body to extract nutrients more completely.

Interestingly, self-reported recovery did not track precisely with the biological measurements. Some athletes in the immediate-bolus group described feeling fully recovered well before their glycogen levels had actually returned to baseline, suggesting that subjective confidence and physiological readiness can diverge. This finding has practical implications for coaches, who may need to rely on measured recovery markers rather than an athlete's own perception when determining readiness for subsequent training sessions.

questions.stem: According to the passage, what did muscle biopsies reveal about the steady-intake group?

options.text: They reported significantly higher levels of fatigue immediately after exercise
They needed a longer overall recovery period
They consumed a greater total volume of fluid during the trial than the other group did
They replenished glycogen faster than the immediate-bolus group

questions.explanationZh: 文中指出穩定補水組肌肉切片顯示肝醣補充速度較快於一次大量補水組，而兩組總攝取量相同，並非攝取量更多、更疲憊或恢復期更長。

questions.stem: The word "bolus" in paragraph 2 most nearly refers to

options.text: a laboratory unit for measuring glycogen stores
a type of connective tissue in muscle fibers
a full dose taken all at once
a scheduled block of time for training

questions.explanationZh: 「bolus」在此指一次性大量攝取的量，對應文中「immediate-bolus group」一次攝取相同容量，並非肌肉結締組織、肝醣測量單位，也不是訓練排程時段。

questions.stem: It can be inferred from the passage that rapid consumption of large fluid volumes

options.text: is generally more effective for muscle recovery than gradual intake
may prevent some nutrients from being fully absorbed
has little to no measurable impact on recovery outcomes
guarantees that athletes will experience noticeable digestive discomfort during recovery

questions.explanationZh: 文中說明快速大量攝取時，部分液體會在養分完全吸收前通過消化系統，可推知這可能導致部分養分無法完全吸收，而非必然造成腸胃不適、效果更好或對恢復毫無影響。

questions.stem: How does the third paragraph relate to the passage as a whole?

options.text: It introduces a distinction between subjective feeling and physiological state
It directly contradicts the study's central finding regarding glycogen replenishment rates across both groups
It outlines the specific methodology and procedures used throughout the controlled trials
It offers historical context for research into athletic hydration practices

questions.explanationZh: 第三段說明部分運動員主觀感覺已恢復，但肝醣值尚未回到基準，點出主觀感受與生理狀態可能不一致，是對全文的補充延伸，並非反駁主要發現、方法摘要或歷史背景介紹。

questions.stem: What is the main purpose of the passage?

options.text: To present research findings on how rehydration timing affects muscle recovery
To criticize coaches for ignoring athlete feedback
To compare glycogen levels across different sports
To argue that athletes should avoid rehydrating during exercise

questions.explanationZh: 全文說明研究如何比較不同補水時機對肌肉恢復的影響，並提出主觀感受與生理狀態可能脫節的發現，主旨在呈現此研究結果，而非主張避免補水、比較運動項目或批評教練。
